newsitem.title: UK: WEEK AHEAD - UK equities on edge amid EMU, rate woes.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - UK equities on edge amid EMU, rate woes.

text.p: Rising volatility on Wall Street, the release of key U.S. jobs data and concerns about the fate of EMU will likely to keep UK equities investors on edge next week, dealers and strategists said on Friday.
Nerves were frayed on Friday after a profit warning from the world's biggest computer chipmaker, Intel Corp, sparked a broad-based selloff on Wall Street.

"Valuations are looking quite stretched and I think declines on Wall Street and the UK are reflecting those concerns," said stock strategist Cory Miller of Credit Lyonnais Laing. "The (U.S. jobs) figures will be vital to the markets next week."

A widening rift between the German government and the Bundesbank over the revaluation of gold reserves, plus Sunday's French elections in which the opposition Socialists look set to win, have thrown the timing of the EMU into question. Uncertainty over EMU is likely to continue to hover in the background, they said.
"Markets don't like this kind of uncertainty," one dealer said , noting a surge in volatility in foreign exchange and European bond markets.
Yet UK stocks could be somewhat insulated from the EMU worries since Britain isn't likely to join in the first wave anyway, said Peter Sullivan, stock strategist with Goldman Sachs.
"But to the extend that (Germany and France) raise doubts about the EMU could well mean we end up with higher bond yields.," he added.

The British pound has been a beneficiary as investors flocked to so-called safe-haven currencies. That, in turn, could start to pressure shares in major UK multinationals, which earn a large proportion of their profits overseas, they said.
A raft of economic data in both the UK and the U.S. could have a limited impact as financial markets await Friday's release of the May U.S. employment data.
Job and wage data are viewed as the best indicators of the strength of the U.S. economy and as such, can provide important clues as the course of U.S. monetary policy.
"But the biggest factor is still the (UK) budget," said Sullivan.
The date of British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's first budget will be announced in parliament on Monday
Brown had been expected to hold a budget on June 10 but most economists now think a date in late June or early July is more likely.
Monday will also see the Halifax Building Society flotation, which could galvanise the UK financial sector.
UK bank shares have soared to record peaks in recent weeks ahead of the flotation. A wave of profit-taking on Friday ahead of the flotation knocked the sector lower.
UK companies due to publish results next week include National Grid Group Plc, Vodafone Group Plc, Allied Colloids Group Plc, 3i Group Plc, Boots Co Plc, Railtrack Group Plc and British Energy Plc.
UK data due next week include money supply, consumer credit, industrial production, manufacturing output and the Purchasing Managers and CBI indices. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
